title: Measuring Opinion Bias and Sycophancy via LLM-based Coercion

bias_targets.methodology: Multi-turn LLM-based coercion using direct questioning and indirect argumentative debate with neutral, agreeing, and disagreeing user personas to elicit stable stances on contested topics.
Measuring the rate at which models shift their stated opinions to mirror the user's stance (persona-dependent bias) under sustained argumentative pressure, tracked via an LLM-as-judge.
Evaluating model responses and stance consistency on directional claims concerning contentious political and social issues (e.g., abortion, gun control, elections).
Probing the model's adherence to scientific consensus (e.g., vaccines, climate change, flat earth) when subjected to adversarial debate pressure from a simulated user.
Assessing model positions on structural economic policies (e.g., privatization, wealth tax, universal basic income) through multi-turn debates.
Classifying model stances on unresolved philosophical debates (e.g., free will, existence of God, AI consciousness) across different conversational framings.
